sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Loathy Lady is a foul and ugly hag from Arthurian legend. She holds the shape of an ancient goddess of sovereignty. A kiss from the rightful king turns her into a blooming young woman. She also calls to mind the Cailleach, the weather-controlling giant of the pre-Celtic age. As a hag she approached the knight Percival and mocked his failure to answer the riddle of the mysterious Fisher King. That loss denied him the sacred Grail that would heal the land. In a noted Arthurian tale she carried the name Ragnell. Ragnell moved between the forms of hag and maiden as the story asked.

okr.objective: Present the Loathy Lady as a sovereignty figure of Arthurian story.
